Verified for real, twice (build failed once on the vite.config.ts bug, fixed, rebuilt clean): WEB_PORT=18080 API_PORT=13000 DB_PORT=15432 docker compose -p erp-system-test up -d --build built both images, all three containers started, db and api reached Healthy before web started (depends_on: condition: service_healthy works). Fully tore down afterward (docker compose down -v --rmi local) and confirmed the machine's 14 pre-existing unrelated containers were untouched. title: Add browser smoke test script
description: Create a repeatable browser smoke test for desktop and mobile demo load. Done 2026-07-17: added playwright as a devDependency (verified it actually launches headless Chromium in this sandbox before committing to the approach -- confirmed working). New scripts/smoke.mjs: expects web/dist/ already built (npm run build:demo), spawns vite preview directly via web/node_modules/.bin/vite (not npx, avoids resolution ambiguity), waits for readiness via actual HTTP polling (not stdout pattern-matching -- found and fixed a real race: vite preview prints its 'Local:' URL before/independent of the socket being ready in some runs), then for both desktop (1280x800) and mobile (375x812) viewports: pre-sets the wizard-complete and demo-auth localStorage flags via page.addInitScript() so the run lands on the dashboard (not the wizard/login -- this is a shell/dashboard smoke test, those flows are covered by TASK-009/007's own manual verification), collects console.error and pageerror events, navigates, waits for .dashgrid to become visible, and asserts document.title mentions the seeded company. Exits 1 with a readable per-viewport report on any error or missing content; kills the preview server in a finally block regardless of outcome. Wired into npm run smoke and into .github/workflows/ci.yml (after build:demo) with proper Playwright browser caching (actions/cache keyed on the playwright version in package.json, install-deps-only on cache hit) so CI doesn't re-download ~170MB of Chromium on every run. Documented in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md. Found and fixed a real bug in the script itself while building it: vite preview binds only the IPv6 loopback ([::1]), not 127.0.0.1 -- the script originally hardcoded 127.0.0.1 and every connection was refused; switched to 'localhost' (lets Node's own resolver pick the right address). Verified all three acceptance criteria directly: (1) confirmed the script starts its own preview server and correctly errors with a clear message if web/dist/ isn't built yet; (2) ran a full pass at both desktop and mobile with zero errors, exit 0; (3) injected a deliberate broken script reference into the built index.html to trigger a real pageerror, confirmed the script correctly reported it per-viewport and exited 1, then restored the clean build and confirmed a passing re-run and a byte-identical rebuild. typecheck/typecheck:web/check:drift/demo/build:demo all still pass.

title: Add purchasing schema and canonical seed
description: First new domain after the sales chain. Add Drizzle schema for supplier, purchase_order, purchase_order_line, goods_receipt (+ supplier invoice posting), all master_fn/company_fn scoped, generated as a proper migration. Implement receiveGoods (stock IN + stock_movement) and supplier-invoice GL posting (AP credit / expense-inventory debit + tax) in src/modules/purchasing, mirroring confirmOrder.ts transaction discipline. Extend src/data/seed.ts and src/demo.ts assertions. Done 2026-07-17: new src/data/schema/purchasing.ts -- supplier (mirrors customer), purchase_order + purchase_order_line (mirrors sales_order/sales_order_line, unitCost instead of unitPrice), goods_receipt, and supplier_invoice (mirrors invoice) -- all master_fn/company_fn scoped with the same tenant-leading composite indexes as sales.ts, generated as drizzle/0002_messy_slyde.sql (23 tables total, confirmed via drizzle-kit's own column/index/fk report). The purchasing lifecycle is modeled as three separate temporal events instead of sales' single confirm-everything-at-once step, matching how real purchasing actually works: (1) createPurchaseOrder.ts -- header+lines+effective-dated tax snapshot, no stock/GL impact, mirrors confirmOrder.ts's line-processing minus the stock-issue call; (2) receiveGoods.ts -- the purchasing-side mirror of inventory/stock.ts's issueStockWithin but incrementing: receives every PO line in one transaction, upserts stock_level via onConflictDoUpdate (creates the row from zero if this is the first-ever stock for that product+warehouse -- verified this specific path, since sales' issueStockWithin only ever assumes a pre-existing row), appends one stock_movement(direction='in') per line, and marks the PO 'received' so it can't be received twice -- that status check is this module's rollback-guard, exercised for real: unguarded would double the stock, guarded rejects with InvalidPurchaseOrderStateError and changes nothing; (3) postSupplierInvoice.ts -- balanced GL (Dr Inventory 1400 + Dr GST/SST Input Tax 1200 = Cr Accounts Payable 2100), mirroring confirmOrder.ts's GL section exactly, gated on the PO already being 'received' (invoicing goods you haven't received is a real accounting error, not just a demo shortcut) -- a second, independent rollback-guard scenario. 8 new vitest cases across 3 test files (createPurchaseOrder/receiveGoods/postSupplierInvoice), including the upsert-from-zero path, a second-PO-adds-onto-existing-stock path, both rollback guards, and a missing-chart-of-accounts PostingError case -- deliberately corrupted two assertions mid-verification to confirm the suite isn't vacuously green (real exit code 1, real diffs), then restored and reconfirmed 36/36. seed.ts gained a supplier (SUPP1, C-SG) and three new chart-of-accounts rows (1400 Inventory, 1200 GST Input Tax, 2100 Accounts Payable) alongside the existing sales-side accounts. demo.ts gained runPurchasingScenario: PO net=120/tax=10.8/total=130.8 (20 widgets @ cost 6, 9% GST), receipt takes stock 0->20 with exactly 1 movement, invoice posts a balanced Dr130.8=Cr130.8 GL, then both rollback guards proven independently (double-receive rejected with stock still 20; invoicing an unreceived second PO rejected with zero GL legs posted) -- wired into the same check() assertion block as the sales scenario, including the cross-engine identity comparison. Re-verified against real PostgreSQL (temporary Docker container, same pattern as docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's dual-adapter section): identical JSON output to PGlite, confirming onConflictDoUpdate's upsert-increment behaves identically on both engines, not just PGlite. web/public/db/erp-system-schema.sql hand-mirrored with the 5 new CREATE TABLE blocks + FK constraints + indexes in the same commit (landmine #1) -- npm run check:drift confirms 23/23 tables match. Deliberately did NOT mirror the new supplier/account SEED DATA into erp-system-seed.sql, and did NOT touch web/public/assets/screens-purchase*.js or either data adapter -- TASK-023 ("mirror the purchasing SQL into web/public/db", "wire purchasing screens to canonical data") explicitly owns that scope; adding unused seed rows or dead screen-wiring now would be scope creep ahead of the task that's supposed to do it. Full local suite green: typecheck, typecheck:web, npm run demo (both engines), npm test (36/36), npm run check:drift, npm run build:demo, npm run smoke, npm run audit:screens (114 routes, zero regressions -- expected, since this task touches no screens or adapters at all).

Done 2026-07-17: scoped to exactly what TASK-022's schema supports -- suppliers, purchase orders, goods receipt, supplier invoice posting -- leaving RFQs/quotations/requisitions/returns/credit-debit-notes/price-lists/landed-cost/vendor-performance/analytics-reports as still-mock (no schema exists for any of those, consistent with how TASK-018 treated every other not-yet-schema-backed module; confirmed via a research agent survey of all 5 purchasing screen files + the 2 mock data files before writing any code, so the scope boundary was a deliberate choice, not an oversight). erp-system-data-adapter.js's readPayload() gained 5 new queries (suppliers/purchaseOrders/purchaseOrderLines/goodsReceipts/supplierInvoices) and applyData() maps them onto DB.suppliers/DB.purchaseOrders/DB.goodsReceipts/DB.supplierInvoices -- code/name/balance and doc/date/status/total are 100% real (balance computed from unpaid supplier_invoice sum, same pattern as customer balance); decorative fields the canonical schema doesn't model (contact, rating, lead-time, buyer, QC disposition, 3-way-match state) are neutral constants, not fake prototype data, so existing list-screen columns don't crash. Added 3 new write functions mirroring confirmOrder's exact raw-SQL transaction pattern (tx.query with $N placeholders, for-update locks, throw-to-rollback, refresh() after commit): createPurchaseOrder (header+lines+tax snapshot), receiveGoods (upsert stock_level via ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE -- verified this creates a stock_level row from zero correctly, not just increments an existing one -- appends stock_movement, guards against double-receiving via the PO status check), postSupplierInvoice (balanced GL, gated on the PO already being received). Wired real actions: screens-purch-new.js's wizard 'Create PO' button now calls createPurchaseOrder for real (was previously a fake toast with a hardcoded PO number that never touched DB.purchaseOrders); also fixed the wizard's hardcoded Kuala-Lumpur-only warehouse list (nonsensical for a Singapore company) to the one real warehouse, and its hardcoded 6% tax preview to the real seeded 9% SG GST rate. screens-purchasing-lists.js's purchase-orders row menu gained real 'Receive goods' and 'Post supplier invoice' actions (status-guarded client-side, matching the adapter's own guards), replacing navigate()-only fakes. Found and fixed two real bugs while browser-testing, not just the planned wiring: (1) DB.suppliers[2] index-based access in screens-fin.js's payment-voucher and screens-ops.js's po-approval risk panel would have crashed once DB.suppliers shrank from the old 4-row mock array to 1 real seeded supplier -- made both defensive with a same-array fallback. Verified the full chain live in-browser end-to-end, twice (once via the pre-seeded PO-1/GR-1/SINV-1, once by creating a brand-new PO-2 through the wizard): Purchase Orders list renders real supplier names/totals/status with zero console errors; created PO-2 for real (toast showed the real generated doc number and total, not a hardcoded placeholder); clicked 'Receive goods' on PO-2 and confirmed SG-WIDGET's on-hand qty visibly increased from 115 to 125 on the actual Inventory > Stock on Hand screen (the exact acceptance criterion); clicked 'Post supplier invoice' and confirmed the General Ledger screen showed a genuinely balanced Dr Inventory 185 + Dr GST Input Tax 16.65 = Cr Accounts Payable 201.65 across both real invoices. Re-ran npm run audit:screens afterward (114 routes, 0 crashes, 0 identity leaks) and npm run smoke to confirm the shared-file changes (screens-fin.js/screens-fin2.js/screens-ops.js) didn't regress anything outside Purchasing. Goods receipt action updates stock on hand visibly in inventory screens

title: Implement minimal real auth against app_user
description: Replace the hardcoded Admin/Superadmin stub (renderLogin in app.js, DB.user in the adapter). Demo mode: auto-login a clearly-labeled demo user, allow switching among seeded users. Production mode: login validates hashed passwords against app_user via the API, session carries master_fn/company_fn/role, company switcher respects user_company. Done 2026-07-17: app_user gained a NOT NULL password_hash column (drizzle/0001_quiet_blizzard.sql). New src/auth/password.ts (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 100k iterations, format pbkdf2$iterations$saltHex$hashHex, timingSafeEqual compare, malformed hashes rejected without throwing) and src/auth/session.ts (in-memory Map<sessionId,SessionData>, httpOnly cookie parsing) -- 13 new vitest cases across password.test.ts/session.test.ts, all passing. src/server.ts: GET /api/setup/status (hasAdmin check, no auth, gates the wizard), POST /api/auth/login (verifyPassword, creates session, sets erp_session httpOnly cookie), POST /api/auth/logout, GET /api/auth/session, and GET /api/dashboard rewritten so masterFn comes ONLY from the session and companyFn is only honored if present in that session's user_company rows (verified via curl: a viewer requesting an unassigned company silently falls back to their own allowed company, no error, no information leakage). Both frontend adapters implement the same needsSetup/isSignedIn/login/logout/switchUser surface so app.js barely branches on mode. erp-system-api-adapter.js redesigned around a 3-state machine (api-unavailable / api-reachable / api) to fix a real chicken-and-egg bug where a reachable-but-logged-out server looked identical to an unreachable one; isSignedIn() now loads the dashboard itself so callers don't need a follow-up step. erp-system-data-adapter.js added hashPasswordBrowser() (Web Crypto PBKDF2, same format as the server), a users query in readPayload(), and activeUser resolution (localStorage flag -> is_superadmin fallback -> first user); the setup wizard now collects+hashes a real admin password (screens-setup-wizard.js, min 8 chars, confirm-match) instead of leaving new users passwordless. seed.ts now creates two real users (admin@acme.co/demo1234, Superadmin on both C-SG and C-MY; viewer@acme.co/viewer1234, Viewer on C-SG only) -- web/public/db/erp-system-seed.sql hand-mirrored to match (landmine #1). scripts/check-drift.mjs upgraded to read drizzle/meta/_journal.json and replay ALL migrations cumulatively (CREATE TABLE / ADD COLUMN / DROP COLUMN), not just 0000_init.sql -- the old single-file assumption would have silently missed this task's own column addition. Verified end-to-end against the full Docker Compose stack (db+api+web, real Postgres): wizard correctly stayed hidden against a seeded database (needsSetup() -> hasAdmin:true), signed in as admin@acme.co, dashboard rendered real session-derived data (name/email, zero hardcoded placeholders), switched company between Acme Singapore and Acme Malaysia (currency/HQ/stock-alert counts changed per company, session-authorized server-side, not client-trusted), signed out, and confirmed 375px mobile rendering -- zero console errors throughout. Two real bugs found and fixed during this verification, not just cosmetic: (1) the login screen's company subtitle read stale mock data ('Northwind Manufacturing') pre-authentication in api mode because DB.company is pre-populated by data-core.js's static template before any adapter runs; fixed app.js's companyLabel to never trust DB.company.name in api mode, always showing plain 'Production' pre-auth. (2) sw.js's staleWhileRevalidate fetch strategy was caching ALL same-origin GET requests including /api/auth/session and /api/dashboard -- the Cache API keys purely on URL and ignores cookies, so after a real server-side logout (confirmed correct in isolation via curl: same cookie jar gets 401 post-logout) the browser still displayed the dashboard because the service worker served back its cached pre-logout 200 response before the network's 401 could matter. Fixed by excluding /api/* and /health from the SW's cache strategy entirely and bumping CACHE_VERSION to v13 so existing installs purge the stale cache on update; re-verified with a real network trace showing POST /api/auth/logout -> 200 immediately followed by GET /api/auth/session -> 401. Also ran the Playwright smoke test (npm run smoke) against the demo build to confirm the shared app.js/sw.js edits didn't regress demo mode -- desktop and mobile both PASS, zero console/page errors. Full local suite green throughout: typecheck, typecheck:web, npm run demo, npm test (28/28), npm run check:drift (0 drift, 18 tables), npm run build:demo. Docker test stack torn down cleanly (down -v --rmi local) with the host's other 13 unrelated containers confirmed untouched by name-list diff. Also fixed an unrelated upstream blocker hit mid-session: a newly-published esbuild@0.28.1 npm release had broken platform-optional-dependency metadata that made npm ci (but not npm install) hard-fail with EBADPLATFORM inside the Docker api build; pinned via package.json overrides.esbuild=0.28.0 and regenerated package-lock.json, verified npm ci clean both locally and in the Docker build.
acceptance: Demo shows a labeled demo user and supports user switching
Password hashes stored (no plaintext) for seeded users
API-mode session scopes every query by master_fn/company_fn from the session
Wizard locks after first admin exists in production mode

description: CONTRIBUTING.md references npm test but no test framework exists; the only gate is src/demo.ts. Add vitest at the root, cover src/modules/sales/confirmOrder.ts (success, insufficient stock rollback, GL balance), src/modules/inventory/stock.ts, and src/data/repo.ts (effective-dated tax) against PGlite in-memory. Add npm test script and document it. Done 2026-07-17: added vitest devDependency + npm test (vitest run). New src/test/helpers.ts (freshDb() -- createPgliteDb + migrate, same pattern as src/demo.ts; every test gets its own isolated in-memory instance, zero shared state, safe to run in any order). 15 tests across 3 files: src/modules/inventory/stock.test.ts (4 -- deduct+one-movement success, InsufficientStockError leaves qty/movements unchanged, negative-stock rejection after a prior issue, exact-boundary qty===available), src/modules/sales/confirmOrder.test.ts (3 -- success with an explicit GL debit==credit==119.9 balance assertion, whole-chain rollback on a later line's insufficient stock INCLUDING the earlier valid line's stock/movements/order/invoice, PostingError when no tax rule covers the order date with the same rollback guarantee), src/data/repo.test.ts (8 -- getEffectiveTaxRate: mid-window, exactly-on validFrom boundary (inclusive), day-before validTo boundary (exclusive), open-ended far-future date, no-match-before-any-rule, no-rule-for-that-code-at-all; addProduct/listProducts: round-trip and tenant-isolation across two different scopes). Fixed the now-stale docs/STATUS.md and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md claims that npm test didn't exist (npm run lint genuinely still doesn't -- left as accurately not-yet-implemented). typecheck/typecheck:web/check:drift/demo/build:demo all still pass alongside the new suite.

title: Wire api-mode frontend to render the real dashboard
description: TASK-011 shipped GET /api/dashboard; TASK-019's erp-system-api-adapter.js deliberately did not call it yet, so VITE_DATA_MODE=api always showed the 'waiting for API' screen even against a live server. Done 2026-07-16: erp-system-api-adapter.js now calls GET {base}/dashboard?masterFn=&companyFn= once health succeeds and maps the response onto DB.company/DB.user/DB.erpSystem/DB.approvals/DB.dashboardMetrics (a deliberately minimal mapper, NOT a full applyData() port -- other modules like inventory/sales/finance have no api-mode data source yet, tracked as real remaining scope, not silently faked). Unmodeled metrics (approvals, glIssues, openDeliveries, goodsReceipts, pickTasks, leaveRequests, cash, cleared) are set to 0 with a comment explaining why, not fabricated. Added switchCompany(companyFn) as a bonus -- it's just a re-fetch with a different companyFn scope, no new server endpoint needed, so the topbar company switcher works in api mode too. Fixed two real bugs found via actual browser verification (not just typecheck): (1) src/data/repo.ts's listCompanies() never selected the currency column at all -- every company in every /api/dashboard response was missing currency, so the UI silently fell back to USD ('$') instead of the correct SGD/MYR ('S$'/'RM'); added `currency: company.currency` to the select. (2) app.js's buildCompanyMenu()/wireCompanyMenu() (from TASK-010) read c.company_fn (snake_case, matching the demo adapter's raw SQL rows) but the api adapter's JSON uses Drizzle's camelCase c.companyFn -- every company button silently got data-co='' in api mode, so clicking any company in the switcher no-op'd (no error, just did nothing) until fixed to `c.company_fn||c.companyFn`. Also made screens-ops.js's erpDemo flag check dataMode!=='api' instead of bare truthiness, so api mode's DB.erpSystem (needed for the company switcher) doesn't trigger the PGlite-only demo narrative text (Beta Pte Ltd, SG-WIDGET, etc) -- zero behavior change for pglite/fallback modes, verified. Verified end-to-end for real via the full Docker Compose stack (not just curl): built+ran+migrated+seeded, dashboard rendered with real figures (S$ correctly, stock-alert count 2 for Singapore vs 1 for Malaysia -- genuinely different per-company data), company switcher worked bidirectionally with zero console errors at desktop and 375px, and the api-unreachable regression path (stopped the api container, fresh browser tab, no stale cache) still correctly showed the honest waiting screen. One incident during verification: a `docker compose up -d api` without repeating the port-override env vars silently recreated the db service on the DEFAULT port 5432, briefly coexisting with the host's already-running Homebrew Postgres (loopback-only bind on the host's side meant no actual data corruption -- verified the host's erp_system_dev database was untouched -- but the ambiguity was caught immediately and fixed by using an explicit --env-file for every subsequent compose command). title: Add CRM schema, business logic, and canonical seed
description: Second new domain after Purchasing (Phase 7 order of attack, docs/ROADMAP.md). Add Drizzle schema for opportunity (tenant-scoped, linked to customer: title, value, currency, stage, probability, close_date, owner) and a lightweight activity log (timestamped note/call linked to an opportunity or customer), generated as a proper migration. Implement a convertOpportunityToSalesOrder-style function in src/modules/crm mirroring confirmOrder.ts/receiveGoods.ts transaction discipline (status guard so an opportunity can't be converted twice, mirroring receiveGoods's open/received guard) -- web/public/assets/data-crm.js's own mock narrative (OPP-26-0091, Meridian Robotics, converts to SO-26-0418) is a ready-made cross-module scenario to model, though the actual seeded demo data/doc numbers should follow this repo's existing Acme/CUST1 seed, not the Aria/Northwind names in that mock file. Extend src/data/seed.ts and src/demo.ts assertions the same way TASK-022 did for purchasing. Done 2026-07-17: new src/data/schema/crm.ts -- opportunity (linked to customer and, optionally, owner_user_id -> app_user and order_id -> sales_order once converted) and activity (lightweight log linked to opportunity), generated as drizzle/0003_fuzzy_ronan.sql (25 tables total). Unlike Purchasing's multi-stage lifecycle, CRM conversion needed to compose with the EXISTING sales module atomically -- an opportunity becoming a sales order and the resulting stock/invoice/GL posting must be ONE transaction, not two sequential ones with a consistency gap between them. confirmSalesOrder (src/modules/sales/confirmOrder.ts) was refactored into a composable confirmSalesOrderWithin(exec, scope, input) core plus a thin confirmSalesOrder(db, scope, input) wrapper -- the exact issueStockWithin/issueStock pattern the codebase already established -- confirmed behavior-preserving for every existing caller (all 3 pre-existing confirmOrder.test.ts cases plus npm run demo's sales scenario re-verified unchanged after the refactor, before writing any new CRM code on top of it). src/modules/crm/createOpportunity.ts is a plain insert (stage defaults 'lead', no line items -- exact SKUs are decided at conversion time, not when a deal is first estimated, matching how real CRM pipelines work and avoiding a redundant opportunity_line table the mock data itself doesn't model). src/modules/crm/convertOpportunityToSalesOrder.ts: one transaction, locks the opportunity row (for update), guards stage not in ('won','lost'), composes confirmSalesOrderWithin, then updates the opportunity to 'won' + links order_id -- all atomic. 7 new vitest cases across 2 files, including the specific test the whole refactor was FOR: a failure inside the composed confirmSalesOrderWithin (insufficient stock) leaves the opportunity completely untouched (still 'lead', order_id still null) rather than half-converted, proving true atomicity rather than two independently-committing steps. Deliberately corrupted one assertion mid-verification (real exit-code-1 failure with a real diff), restored, reconfirmed clean. seed.ts gained one opportunity (OPP-1, CUST1, 'negotiation' stage, deliberately left unconverted so the eventual TASK-028 UI has an in-flight pipeline deal to show) -- demo.ts's runCrmScenario creates a SEPARATE opportunity (OPP-2) and converts it for the proof, leaving the seed's OPP-1 untouched, mirroring how runPurchasingScenario creates its own fresh PO rather than reusing anything from seedDemo. Full CRM chain proven on both PGlite and real PostgreSQL (temporary Docker container): conversion creates a real order (net=50/tax=4.5/total=54.5), stock 50->45, balanced GL, both rollback guards (double-convert rejected; insufficient-stock-inside-the-composed-transaction leaves the opportunity at its original 'lead' stage), and the .for('update') row lock on opportunity confirmed to behave identically on both engines. Found and fixed 2 real, unrelated issues while working in this area: (1) a genuinely unused import (InvalidPurchaseOrderStateError, TASK-022's own leftover, referenced only inside a comment, silently allowed since this tsconfig doesn't enable noUnusedLocals) -- removed. (2) A real test-suite flakiness risk: vitest's default 5000ms testTimeout was occasionally insufficient once a 4th migration meant every freshDb() call replays more DDL, and running all 10 test files concurrently (vitest's default) under load intermittently pushed some PGlite WASM boots past that timeout -- reproduced (8/10 files failed on one run, 1/10 on another, both times as freshDb() itself timing out, never a real assertion failure), then fixed with a new vitest.config.ts (testTimeout: 20000) and confirmed 3 consecutive full-suite runs clean afterward. web/public/db/erp-system-schema.sql hand-mirrored with the 2 new tables in the same commit (landmine #1) -- npm run check:drift confirms 25/25 tables match. No screens or adapter touched -- TASK-028 owns that scope, matching the TASK-022/023 split. Full local suite green: typecheck, typecheck:web, npm run demo (both engines), npm test (40/40), npm run check:drift, npm run build:demo, npm run smoke, npm run audit:screens (114 routes, zero regressions).
acceptance: Drizzle migration adds opportunity (+ activity log) with tenant-scoped indexes
Every opportunity links to a real customer row
Converting an opportunity creates a real sales_order in one transaction, rejecting a second conversion of the same opportunity

title: Wire CRM screens to canonical data
description: Replace the Aria/Northwind mock CRM data (data-crm.js) with adapter reads from the new CRM tables, following the exact pattern TASK-023 established for Purchasing: readPayload()/applyData() additions in erp-system-data-adapter.js, a real write function mirroring confirmOrder's transaction pattern exposed on window.ErpSystemDemo, mirror the CRM seed/txn SQL into web/public/db/erp-system-seed.sql and erp-system-demo-txn.sql, and wire the pipeline board's 'Convert to sales order' action (screens-crm.js's opportunity screen and crm-pipeline board) to the real adapter call instead of a toast. Leave any CRM sub-features with no schema backing (if scope grows beyond opportunity+activity during TASK-027) on mock data, consistent with how Purchasing's RFQs/quotations/etc stayed mock. Pipeline board, opportunity detail, and customer-360 views run against PGlite in demo mode. Done 2026-07-17: erp-system-data-adapter.js gained an opportunities query in readPayload() (joins customer + app_user for owner name/email) and a DB.pipeline builder in applyData() that groups by stage (lead/qualified/proposal/negotiation/won) into the same {stage,items[]} shape the existing screens-crm.js kanban already expected, deriving avatar initials from the owner name instead of hardcoded mock avatars. Two new adapter functions mirror the createPurchaseOrder/receiveGoods pattern: createOpportunity(input) (plain insert, doc-numbered via the existing nextDocNo helper) and convertOpportunityToSalesOrder(opportunityNo, sku, qty, unitPrice) (SQL port of convertOpportunityToSalesOrder.ts -- locks the opportunity row, guards won/lost, runs the same confirmOrder steps inline, then marks the opportunity won+linked, all as one transaction). screens-crm-new.js's wizard now posts through createOpportunity instead of a toast-only stub (also fixed a latent bug: the deal-value field label was hardcoded 'Deal value (USD)' regardless of company currency). screens-crm.js's kanban cards gained a convert button (hidden on Won cards) opening a new modal (item/qty/unit-price, with a suggested qty derived from the opportunity's estimated value) that calls convertOpportunityToSalesOrder with the established disable-button/try-catch/toast/navigate pattern. erp-system-seed.sql gained the OPP-1 insert TASK-027 already had in seed.ts (this file is a separate hand-mirror per landmine #1 and had been missed -- the pipeline board rendered '0 open / No deals' in every column until this was added). erp-system-demo-txn.sql gained a third DO block mirroring demo.ts's runCrmScenario: creates OPP-2 (separate from the seed's own still-open OPP-1, matching how runCrmScenario itself never touches the seeded opportunity) and converts it inline (net=50, tax=4.5, total=54.5, stock-5), giving the demo a pre-populated 'Won' column on first load the same way SO-1/PO-1 are pre-processed Sales/Purchasing examples. All 3 DO blocks in that file (sales, purchasing, now CRM) verified together against a disposable PostgreSQL container (docker run postgres:16-alpine, schema+seed+txn piped through psql) -- zero errors, and the resulting data matches exactly: opportunity table has OPP-1/negotiation (untouched) and OPP-2/won/order_id=2; sales_order has SO-CRM-1 net=50/tax=4.5/total=54.5; SG-WIDGET stock at WH-SALES = 110 (100 seed -5 SO-1 +20 PO-1 -5 SO-CRM-1); every gl_entry journal_ref sums debit=credit exactly. Found and fixed one real, pre-existing bug while doing live browser verification (unrelated to CRM specifically, but only surfaced because this task's seed/txn payload pushed boot time over the edge): erp-system-data-adapter.js's boot orchestration raced a 20s watchdog against bootPglite() via a one-shot applyOnce() lock -- if the watchdog fired first and applied the static fallback payload, bootPglite() finishing successfully afterward was silently discarded (applied stayed true forever), so the UI could get permanently stuck on stale mock data with no user-visible error and no recovery short of a manual reset. Root-caused live: a leftover browser tab from earlier verification had an open PGlite/IndexedDB connection that blocked every new tab's bootPglite() from ever completing before the watchdog fired -- closing that tab unblocked boot immediately. Fixed applyOnce() to allow exactly one fallback-to-pglite override (never the reverse) and, when that late override happens, re-navigate the currently-displayed route so the swap is actually visible instead of sitting correct-but-unpainted in DB. Full interactive verification in-browser after the fix: pipeline board renders OPP-1 (Negotiation, S$5,000/75%) and OPP-2 (Won, S$65/70%) from real PGlite data; created a new opportunity (OPP-3) via the wizard, landed correctly in the Lead column; converted OPP-1 via the new modal -- first deliberately entered a qty (769) exceeding on-hand stock to confirm the InsufficientStockError path surfaces a clear toast and leaves the modal open with the opportunity untouched, then retried with qty=8 (SO-CRM-5 created, S$56.68), confirmed visible in Sales > Sales Orders (not just CRM), stock decremented 110->102, and GL balanced (Dr AR 231 = Cr Revenue 212 + Cr GST Output 19; Dr Inventory 120 + Dr GST Input 11 = Cr AP 131). Checked crm-pipeline and new-opportunity at 375px: zero console errors, no layout breakage. Full local suite green: typecheck, typecheck:web, npm test (40/40), npm run check:drift (25/25 tables), npm run demo (both engines, CRM scenario included), npm run build:demo, npm run smoke, npm run audit:screens (114 routes, zero regressions, no leftover Northwind/Dana Reyes markers).
acceptance: CRM routes render canonical PGlite data with zero console errors
Converting an opportunity creates a real sales order visible in Sales screens (and increments there, not just in CRM)
No hardcoded Northwind CRM figures remain
Desktop and 375px widths verified
